title: docs(fields): `lookup.mdx` / `user.mdx` author `lookupFilters` operators in the spec's DEPRECATED alias spellings (`eq`, `ne`) — the canonical vocabulary is `equals` / `not_equals`
body:
Found by the objectui#7713 dev (PM loop R44, `domain:devx` seat) while rewriting the `object-grid` filter example on `content/docs/guide/objectos-integration.mdx`. Filed unassigned; ⛔ NOT fixed in that PR — different pages, different key, outside that card's scope fence. Written by an agent session (`session_013uAaxiwgYDybsTNV9xwa1M`); attribution is in this sentence on purpose.

## Measured on `origin/main` at `859de84a0` (2026-09-06)

Two field-reference pages author a `lookupFilters` rule with an operator spelling the spec classifies as DEPRECATED:

```
content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx:43   lookupFilters: [{ field: 'active', operator: 'eq', value: true }],
content/docs/fields/user.mdx:43     lookupFilters: [{ field: 'banned', operator: 'ne', value: true }],
```

`eq` and `ne` are not members of the canonical vocabulary. Measured by importing the shipped spec in this repo's `node_modules`:

```
VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS = ["equals","not_equals","contains","not_contains","icontains",
  "starts_with","ends_with","greater_than","less_than","greater_than_or_equal",
  "less_than_or_equal","in","not_in","is_empty","is_not_empty","is_null","is_not_null",
  "before","after","between"]

normalizeFilterOperator('eq') === 'equals'
normalizeFilterOperator('ne') === 'not_equals'
```

Both live only in `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES`, whose own doc comment in `@objectstack/spec` states the rule verbatim:

> These are historical shorthand (`eq`, `gt`) and camelCase (`notEquals`, `greaterThan`) forms that older authoring tools and already-stored view metadata may still carry. … Deprecated: new producers MUST emit the canonical forms; these aliases are a migration bridge and may be dropped in a future major.

A documentation example is a new producer: every reader who copies it emits a deprecated spelling.

## Why nothing catches it

Both blocks type-check, because `normalizeFilterOperator` takes `unknown` and the surrounding literals are not annotated against a type that carries the operator enum. `check:doc-snippets` compiles the fence and is green; the enum is never consulted. This is the same "no reader is consulted" shape as objectui#7713, one layer milder — the alias still lowers correctly TODAY, so the cost is a future major dropping the bridge, not wrong rows now.

## Suggested repair (docs only, mechanical)

`operator: 'eq'` to `operator: 'equals'`, `operator: 'ne'` to `operator: 'not_equals'`. No prose change, no runtime change — the lowering is byte-identical either way. Verify with `pnpm check:doc-snippets` and `pnpm check:doc-types`.

⛔ Not measured here, so not a claim: whether `lookupFilters` itself is a declared key on the field schemas the two pages document. objectui#7021 records that the concept exists in two spellings (`lookup_filters` / `lookupFilters`); that is a different card and this one does not touch it.

Related: objectui#7713 (the same "the docs teach a spelling no contract endorses" class, on `object-grid.filter`), objectui#7021, objectui#7537 (another `lookup.mdx` prose-vs-spec row).
